h1: The 6 Best Cross-Platform Bluetooth Trackers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 cross-platform Bluetooth trackers that work with iPhone and Android, compared on networks, battery, loudness and water rating.
summary: The UGREEN Finder Duo Air 4-pack is the best cross-platform tracker: it joins Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, recharges over USB-C for about 365 days per charge and carries Apple and Google certification. The Arleedyn is the loudest and most rugged tag, the Reyke offers 180 ft of range, and the KIUP is the slimmest for a wallet.
intro: Cross-platform trackers are a recent invention, and most buyers do not realize what the label means. A tag that works with both iPhone and Android usually does not join both networks at once: you pick Apple Find My or Google Find Hub during setup, and that choice decides whose phones help locate it. Switching later often means a reset. Choose the network that matches the phones around the person who loses the item.

We ranked six trackers that list support for both ecosystems, covering a four-tag set, a wallet card and a Tile pack. The scoring weighed certification, battery design, loudness, water rating and how the tag attaches to real objects. Specs come from the listings, and we mark where a number, such as battery life, is a seller claim that we could not corroborate.

products.name: UGREEN Finder Duo Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack
products.verdict: Four rechargeable tags with 365 days per USB-C charge, Apple and Google certification and end-to-end encryption.
products.description:
UGREEN's Finder Duo Air is certified by both Apple and Google and joins either Apple Find My or Google Find Hub. The tags are rechargeable over universal USB-C and last 365 days per charge, a design that avoids the disposable coin cell. End-to-end encryption, Lost Mode and alerts complete the feature set.

It ranks first because it removes the battery problem and keeps both certifications. The coioc uses a replaceable battery instead, which suits those who dislike charging. Against the Reyke, it lists no range figure but offers rechargeable convenience. The listing places it in the $25 to $50 bucket for four tags.

Best for households that want one set of tags with minimal upkeep. The caveat is that a rechargeable tag needs a charge every year, so set a reminder.

products.name: Arleedyn 2026 Air Tags 4 Pack for Android and iOS
products.verdict: A 100 dB alarm, IP68 waterproofing and 0.28 oz weight, with cases and lanyards in the box.
products.description:
Arleedyn packs a 100 dB alarm into a tag that weighs 0.28 oz each, and the IP68 water rating covers immersion beyond the IP67 tags. Setup lets you choose the Apple or the Google network. In the box are four cases, four lanyards and four opening tools, so the tags attach to keys and bags immediately.

It ranks second because loudness and the IP68 rating matter in the real world, and the included cases save a separate purchase. The KIUP's 120 dB speaker is louder, but it is a wallet card. Against the UGREEN, the Arleedyn lists no battery life, which is the missing number that keeps it below first.

Best for keys, bags and gear that get wet. The caveat is the unstated battery life, so ask the seller before relying on it.

products.name: Reyke 2026 Dual-System Tracker Tags 4-Pack
products.verdict: Apple MFi and Google certified, up to 180 ft of Bluetooth range, sharing with up to 5 users and no subscription.
products.description:
Reyke lists certification from Apple MFi and Google, a Bluetooth range of up to 180 ft, and sharing with up to five users plus the owner. It needs Android 9 or newer, or iOS 14 or newer, and there is no subscription. It joins Apple Find My or Google Find Hub.

It ranks third because the range figure is a best-case number and the listing is thinner on battery detail than the UGREEN. Against the coioc, which lists 120 ft, the Reyke claims 50% more range, which matters mostly in open spaces. Sharing for up to five people suits a family, and the no-subscription note is a plus.

Best for families sharing tags. The caveat is that open-air range collapses indoors, so treat 180 ft as theoretical.

products.name: coioc Air Tracker Tags 4-Pack, Find Hub and Find My
products.verdict: Certified by Apple and Google, IP67 waterproof, with a replaceable battery and 120 ft range.
products.description:
coioc is certified by Apple and Google and joins either Google Find Hub or Apple Find My. The battery is replaceable, the IP67 rating covers rain and short immersion, and the Bluetooth range is listed at up to 120 ft. A sharing mode lets another person see the tag.

It ranks fourth because the IP67 rating is a step below the Arleedyn's IP68 and it lists no alarm volume. Against the UGREEN, the replaceable cell is the trade: you swap batteries instead of charging. The pack of four sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, the same as the three above.

Best for people who prefer swapping a coin cell. The caveat is that the listing gives no battery life, so you do not know how often you will swap.

products.name: KIUP Wallet Tracker Card, Find My and Find Hub
products.verdict: A 0.06 inch thin card with a speaker up to 120 dB, IP68 waterproofing and UWB distance display.
products.description:
KIUP is built to sit in a wallet slot: 0.06 inch thick, IP68 waterproof, with a speaker rated up to 120 dB and a UWB distance display. Either Apple's or Google's network can be chosen at setup. The listing claims a battery life of 5 to 10 years, a claim we treat with caution until owners confirm it.

It ranks fifth because one card is not a set, and the wallet form factor serves one job. The 120 dB speaker is louder than the Arleedyn's 100 dB, which helps in a loud bag. UWB distance display adds precision finding. It costs under $25.

Best for wallets and passport holders. The caveat is the seller's 5 to 10 year battery claim, which is unusually long.
products.idealFor: People who want a wallet tracker that fits a card slot.
products.skipIf: You need to track keys or bags.

products.name: Life360 Tile Bluetooth Tracker 4-Pack
products.verdict: Works on iOS and Android through the Tile app and network, rings your phone and adds an SOS alert.
products.description:
Tile works on iOS and Android using its own app and network, not Apple Find My or Google Find Hub. It rings your phone even when silenced, includes a discreet SOS alert and ties into the Life360 family map. The pack of four costs $50 to $100.

Last place follows from its network is independent of the two big ones, so finding depends on how many Tile users are nearby. The certified tags above tap Apple and Google's networks. What Tile offers instead is a mature app, the phone-finding feature and the Life360 link for families.

Best for families already on Life360. The caveat is the higher price for four tags and a smaller finding network.
products.idealFor: Families already using Life360 who want trackers tied into the same app.
products.skipIf: You want Apple or Google's network to help find items.

whatMatters.detail: A dual-system tag joins Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, not both. Pick the one that matches the phones around the person who loses things. Check the listing for the phrase Find My or Find Hub, and look for the certification wording, because uncertified tags may not work reliably.

Apple MFi and Google certification mean the tag has been checked against each platform's rules for privacy and anti-stalking alerts. The UGREEN, Reyke and coioc list both. Tags without certification may behave unpredictably, so prefer listings that name both. Certification also governs the alerts that warn you about an unknown tag traveling with you, so it protects privacy as well as reliability.

Rechargeable tags, such as the UGREEN's 365 days per USB-C charge, need a yearly top-up, while replaceable cells need a swap. A 5 to 10 year battery claim, as on the KIUP, is a seller number. Check whether the listing names the battery type and life. Seller figures of many years deserve skepticism, so favor a design you can recharge or open and refresh yourself.

A 100 dB alarm, as on the Arleedyn, is audible through a bag, while quieter tags are not. IP68 survives deeper immersion than IP67. Look for decibel and IP figures, and ignore vague phrases like waterproof design. A louder speaker helps most when the tag is buried under a coat or inside a bag, where quiet chirps vanish completely.

The Reyke needs Android 9 or newer, or iOS 14 or newer. Older phones may not support the network features. Check your phone's OS version against the listing before buying a four-pack. Older handsets may pair but lose features such as alerts or sharing, which defeats the point of a family set. Open the phone's settings and read the version number first.

faq.q: Can one tag work with iPhone and Android at the same time?
faq.a: Not on both networks. Dual-system tags such as the UGREEN and Reyke join Apple Find My or Google Find Hub at setup. Pick the one that matches the phones around you.

faq.q: What is the biggest cross-platform tracker mistake?
faq.a: Buying uncertified tags. The UGREEN, Reyke and coioc list Apple and Google certification, while many generic tags do not. Certification also affects anti-stalking alerts.

faq.q: Is the Arleedyn worth it over the UGREEN?
faq.a: If your gear gets wet or lost in loud places, yes. It offers a 100 dB alarm and IP68 rating, but lists no battery life. The UGREEN trades that for rechargeable convenience.

faq.q: How do I switch a tag between iPhone and Android?
faq.a: Reset it following the maker's instructions, then pair it again to the other network. The Reyke needs Android 9 or iOS 14 and newer. Expect to lose shared access when you reset.

faq.q: How often do I need to charge or replace the battery?
faq.a: The UGREEN lists 365 days per charge. The coioc has a replaceable cell with no life stated. The KIUP claims 5 to 10 years, a figure to treat cautiously.

faq.q: Will a wallet card tracker fit in any wallet?
faq.a: The KIUP is 0.06 inch thick, thin enough for most card slots. It tracks the wallet, not the keys, so pair it with a tag set such as the Arleedyn for the rest.

finalTake: For most mixed households the UGREEN Finder Duo Air 4 Pack is the best cross-platform tracker: Apple and Google certification, a rechargeable battery and four tags. The Arleedyn is the pick for loud, waterproof gear, the Reyke for shared family use, and the KIUP card for wallets.
